input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 runs in the wrong direction: it is a reverse MFN obliging Customer to disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable third-party commercial offer, with no product limitation, no time limit and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs. That is the walk-away position (an open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor) and fails every fallback element. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and negate the obligation in Section 7.2 rather than trying to bound it, which removes the conflict with Section 12.3. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing in Customer's favour is affected.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives from another provider.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the reverse most-favoured-nation obligation in Section 7.2, so we no longer have to disclose or match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit. Our position is that Customer takes on no MFN obligation, consistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Turn Section 7.2's Customer-side match obligation into an express no-MFN statement.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
